title: Physics: Mechanics for Biomedical Engineers
description: Kinematics, forces, energy, momentum, rotation, and material response taught through free-body diagrams and experimental checks.

prerequisites.statement: Algebra and trigonometry; calculus taken concurrently

outcomes.description: Build a free-body diagram with consistent axes.
Apply conservation laws and Newton's laws.
Quantify torque, angular momentum, and rotational energy.
Check mechanical predictions against units and limiting cases.

lesson_objectives.description: Translate position data into velocity and acceleration.
Apply Newton's second law along chosen axes.
Use work-energy when forces vary with position.
Distinguish conservative energy storage from dissipation.
Apply momentum conservation to a defined isolated system.
Calculate torque about a stated axis.
Relate stress and strain to a material model.

workload.basis: Not measured. Legacy nominal credit and display-time labels are not retained as workload estimates.

lessons.title: Kinematics and force balance
lessons.worked_example: A 0.20 kg instrument package accelerating upward at 2 m/s² has tension T−mg=ma, so T=0.20(9.81+2)=2.36 N.

lessons.title: Work, energy, and power
lessons.worked_example: Compressing a linear spring by x stores U=½kx². A spring with k=200 N/m compressed 0.05 m stores 0.25 J.

lessons.title: Momentum, collisions, and impulse
lessons.worked_example: A 0.15 kg ball changes velocity from +8 to −4 m/s. Its impulse is 0.15(−12)=−1.8 N·s.

lessons.title: Rotation, torque, and material response
lessons.worked_example: A 10 N force perpendicular to a 0.25 m lever arm produces 2.5 N·m torque.

grading_policy.attempt_policy: Unlimited formative retries; no summative grade is awarded.
grading_policy.solution_release: Public practice solutions may be shown after an attempt. They are not production exam keys.
grading_policy.late_policy: No deadlines or late penalties exist in this partial package.
grading_policy.appeals: No instructor review workflow is implemented; report ambiguous practice items to repository maintainers.

accessibility.diagram_policy: The seed package contains no imported diagrams; newly authored diagrams require descriptions and individual license tracking.
known_issues: Unicode equations require structured mathematical alternatives and assistive-technology review.

history.summary: Preserved original compact prototype content in separate manifests and readings; labeled partial without semester or credit equivalency.

limitations: Four compact legacy units are preserved; this package is not equivalent to a full university semester.
There is no authored 12–15 week schedule, substantive homework sequence, laboratory sequence, midterm, cumulative final, or graded integrative project.
The single formative check per lesson does not demonstrate comprehensive outcome coverage or mastery; association with the first lesson objective is provisional.
Bloom labels and structured prerequisite edges are initial authoring classifications awaiting subject-matter review.
Question answers and solution feedback are intentionally public practice authoring specifications, not restricted exam keys.
Numerical specifications preserve the prototype's tolerance and optional unit entry; significant-figure and dimensional checks have not been authored.
Total workload and weekly duration are unknown; former nominal credit values and hardcoded reading times do not establish workload.
intentionally_omitted: Full instructional sequence and summative assessments are not authored yet; this is a preserved seed inventory.
